title: Creditor Rights, Bank-Borrower Relationships and Bank Power
authors: Marco Ghitti; Florencio Lopez-de-Silanes; Rafael Almeida da Matta
eligible_reason: Table III rows A1-A2 report Callaway-Sant'Anna estimates (csdid, no covariates) on a firm-quarter panel with a binary absorbing treatment switching on at firm-specific quarters (first quarter the firm's rating exceeds the median), with never-treated (A1) or not-yet-treated (A2) controls and multiple cohorts (2010q1-2014q2). PROTOCOL Sec. 2 makes explicitly reported CSA estimates of such a design eligible; a TWFE counterpart (Id_Debtor + Quarter FE) can be constructed. Caveat: this 'treatment' is the firm's risk status, used by the authors as a robustness device, whereas the headline design (High Risk x continuous creditor-rights index with controls) is ineligible.
design_notes: Universe of corporate credits of a large Italian bank, 2009q4-2014q2, credit-level and firm-level quarterly panels (not shipped). Main specs: xtreg y credit controls firm controls Exp2_CC Exp2_CRI i.Quarter i.Industry i.Sisba_Family i.Segment_Size i.Prov, fe i(Id_Debtor) vce(cluster Id_Debtor). Table III robustness rows: A1/A2 csdid with gvar treated; A3 firm-level baseline with controls; B-I alternative treatment definitions (High Risk x Reform 2010 dummies), macro interactions, clustering, subsamples. Figures: csdid event-study plots.
estimators_reported: TWFE with continuous treatment intensity and controls (xtreg fe)
reghdfe with two-way clustering (Table III F)
main_or_robustness: robustness (CSA rows in main-text Table III; main design is continuous-intensity)
modern_estimators_named: Callaway-Sant'Anna (csdid, dripw; never-treated and not-yet-treated controls)

specs.treatment_definition: treated = quarter in which the firm first becomes High Risk (bank internal rating above the median), 0 before and for firms never high-risk (comment in robustness_reg_replication.do line 71: 'dummy equal to 1 from the first quarter when a firm is treated (i.e High Risk > median) and 0 before'); absorbing by construction. Cohorts span Stata quarters 200-217 (2010q1-2014q2) per the log (groups g200..g214 listed).
specs.fe: Callaway-Sant'Anna group-time ATTs (csdid default dripw), no covariates; TWFE counterpart would use Id_Debtor + Quarter FE
specs.sample_condition: credit_firm_data_CS.dta: firm-quarter panel aggregated from credit-level data of one large Italian bank; unbalanced panel (csdid uses pair-balanced observations)
specs.static_or_event: static (estat simple; dynamic ATTs also printed in log)
specs.reported_location: Table III, rows A1 (never-treated control) and A2 (not-yet-treated control)
specs.notes: csdid y, ivar(Id_Debtor) time(Quarter) gvar(treated) [notyet]; estat simple. Reported as a robustness row of the main-text Table III; the paper's headline design (Tables II, IV-VI) is High Risk x CRI (continuous creditor-rights index) with controls and is ineligible. Treatment here is an endogenous firm state (becoming high-risk), not a policy; lead to judge whether this counts as the paper's DiD design.

data_files: No data shipped (bank NDA); log_MainTables.smcl and log_RobustnessTables.smcl contain full output; data dictionary PDF
screener_notes: Screened from package only (readme PDF, main_reg_replication.do, robustness_reg_replication.do, logs). Treatment variable 'treated' is defined only in a code comment; the construction script is not shipped.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Quarterly cohorts 2010q1-2014q2 (groups g200, g210, g214 among others visible in the log); exact count not recoverable without data.
software_notes: Stata SE 15.1 (17.0 for Table I); xtreg, reghdfe, csdid, estout
priority_note: Eligible CSA rows but data unavailable; estimates recoverable from logs.
